episode_summary: Episode 363 (August 2021): a roundtable of the hosts on the Poly Network hack of about $600 million and the hacker's returns, a US infrastructure-bill provision that would have covered wallet software, the New York BitLicense, China's BSN network, the London upgrade's ether burn, USDC backing, DeFi token proliferation, and crypto's energy use.

cards.claim: In August 2021 about $600 million was stolen in a hack of the Poly Network, which the hosts called the largest hack of all time.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: $600 million stolen from the Polygon Network

cards.claim: In August 2021 the Poly Network hacker reportedly returned about $120 million of the stolen funds.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: And he's given back, I think, $120 million of it because he feels bad.

cards.claim: The hosts recalled the Mt. Gox hack as roughly 850,000 bitcoin, worth about $450 million at the time.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It was $450 million at the time, but 850,000 Bitcoins.

cards.claim: In August 2021 the Poly Network hacker reportedly sent $48,200 worth of ether to a person who warned him that stolen tether would be blacklisted.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Here's $48,200 worth of ether.

cards.claim: In August 2021 the Poly Network hacker was reportedly trying to work with the Polygon team to return the stolen funds.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: he's trying to work with the Polygon team to give it back

cards.claim: In August 2021 a proposed clause in the US infrastructure bill would have treated anyone touching crypto, including personal wallet developers, as a money services provider.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: they tried to squeeze in some legislation that would mean that like you have to keep track of like you become a money services provider

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host said his company, which runs a non-custodial wallet, offered no services in the United States and operated from Singapore.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: My company doesn't offer services to the United States.

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host argued the New York BitLicense, authored by a regulator, stifled crypto development in New York and protected the stock market.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: right after he authored and pushed through the BitLicense in New York, which essentially stifled all development in New York

cards.claim: After the BitLicense, many crypto services said they served Americans except in New York, a point the hosts raised in August 2021.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: yeah, we offer service to Americans except for New York

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host said the BitLicense required almost $750,000 of capital to run a Bitcoin business in New York.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it says pretty much you need like almost three quarters of a million dollars just to have a Bitcoin business in New York

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host warned that China was investing heavily in blockchain infrastructure over the next decade or two in order to control it.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: because they're dumping a tremendous amount of money in blockchain

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host explained the Blockchain Services Network (BSN) as China's central hub through which blockchains would connect.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Blockchain Services Network. That's what China's central hub that all the blockchain is connected to.

cards.claim: In August 2021 the hosts said the infrastructure bill hoped to raise roughly $50 to $200 billion from crypto taxes alone.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: they're hoping to raise like something like 50 to 200 something billion dollars from crypto taxes alone

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host argued DeFi had grown fast on a technology stack that was not yet ready for the money it handled.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Look at how fast DeFi has blown up on a technology stack that isn't ready for that kind of money yet.

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host argued the US gained an edge by not overregulating the automobile, unlike England, and warned crypto could face the same mistake.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: But all across the pond over in England, they overregulated the automobile.

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host warned that overregulating crypto would leave America behind other countries.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I hope legislators wake up and realize that if we are hard, take a hard line of not knowing what we're doing and overregulate crypto

cards.claim: In August 2021, after the London upgrade, the hosts said ether was being burned in fees at a fast rate.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: there's been an ether burn been burning ether like it's going out of style

cards.claim: In August 2021 Coinbase reportedly removed its claim that USDC was backed by US dollars.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: So Coinbase removes backed by US dollars claim for USDC stablecoin.

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host explained fractional reserve banking as a bank holding less cash than its deposit liabilities, and compared stablecoin backing to it.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: fractional reserve banking is like hey i don't have enough money in this bank to even support the number of deposits that i have

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host said many DeFi projects minted tokens with no real value, a sign that crypto was repeating its own mistakes.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: everybody's running up defy projects that essentially mint random ass tokens for nothing

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host argued Bitcoin's appeal had been its limited supply, which DeFi was abandoning.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the crypto that we were talking about bitcoin specifically it was cool because it was limited

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host said EIP-1559's fee burn had made ether deflationary, giving it some of Bitcoin's properties.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: you essentially have made Ether deflationary overnight

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host argued that crypto networks, after a decade, all centralize in some way despite being designed to be decentralized.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: all of these networks centralize in some way, shape, or form

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host defended Bitcoin mining's energy use as turning energy into money for a potential global currency.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: because we're turning energy into money and potentially a main currency system that runs on the planet

cards.claim: In August 2021 a host said NFTs were about more than JPEGs on a hard drive, pointing to decentralized storage such as the interplanetary filing system (IPFS).
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: NFTs aren't just about JPEGs stored on someone's hard drive.

cards.claim: In August 2021 the hosts pointed listeners to ultrasound.money to track the Ethereum burn.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: is a website where you can see how quickly the Ethereum burn is happening

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #363-The Bridge Over The Poly Network
